1	# Rules: Project Landing Page
2	
3	- **R-v7q.** A project's Needs you lists the same things Home does, for that project alone, newest first, and isn't shown when nothing needs the person there.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
5	- **R-2hx.** A design with a branch is listed under In progress and not under Designs; once its branch is finished, it's listed under Designs again.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
7	- **R-k4n.** Pushing a branch is always asked first, saying which branch goes to which remote, and nothing is pushed until the person says yes.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:project/branches/:branch/publish @ typical*
9	- **R-8dz.** The page's work and its app follow what happens elsewhere without a reload: a turn, a build, a push or a merge changes them as it happens, and they're read again every five minutes for what Prelude can't see, such as a pull request merged on the Git server.
10	- **R-wm3.** New design offers the design system and the app shell as kinds only until the project has one of each.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:project/designs/new @ new-project*
12	- **R-r6b.** A design under Designs says it's ready to build when it has approved pages not yet built, and only once the project's app exists. A design that changed since it was approved isn't ready: it says it changed, until it's approved again.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
14	- **R-h2w.** Once the app is built, it can be run from the project's own folder with a command and address of its own, never the design host's, and the Run button always shows the command it runs, so clicking it is the approval.
15	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
16	- **R-p7c.** Building or connecting the app sets how it runs from here, so a newly built app can be run without setting anything; a command changed on this page applies on this computer only.
17	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
18	- **R-5tj.** The app run from here opens in the browser once it answers at its address, and stops when Prelude quits.

1	# Project Landing Page - notes
2	
3	A project's own page (`/f/<id>`), a redesign of `server/views/_folder.eta` (with
4	`_branch.eta`), whose model is built in `server/main.js` (`view()` in the
5	`/f/:id` handler). Home (prelude/landing-page) gathers what needs the person
6	across projects and links here; this page holds the project's whole picture.
7	
8	Pages: `/f/:project` (Project), `/f/:project/designs/new` (New design, modal),
9	`/f/:project/branches/:branch/publish` (Push a branch, modal),
10	`/f/:project/cleanup` (Clean up, modal), `/f/:project/branches/:branch/discard`
11	(Discard a branch, modal). Fragments:
12	`/f/:project/work`, `/f/:project/app`. States: typical (spark-lending), new
13	project, app being built, update clashed (with the app on the shell's branch
14	and a failed push), long names (an existing app to connect, no remote),
15	large project (a hundred features).
16	
17	## Decisions (the person asked for all eleven, 2026-10-18)
18	
19	1. **On the design system**, not ds/v1 + `prelude.css`, like Home.
20	2. **Work beside setup**: a `.split` in a `.center.wide`. Main: Needs you, In
21	   progress, Designs. Side: The app, What the agent can read. Added
22	   `.center.wide` / `--measure-wide` to the design system (46rem can't hold a
23	   split).
24	3. **New design is a modal**, opened by the header's "New design…", the page's
25	   one primary action. A refused title comes back into the fields alone
26	   (`_new-design-fields`); made, the modal closes and the page refreshes (the
27	   real app opens the new design's page).
28	4. **One primary per view**: Merge, Push, Start the app build are plain buttons.
29	5. **A branch's state as pills**: check, building / build stopped, behind main,
30	   pull request open, nothing done yet. Stories get a state pill (Built, To
31	   build, Building) and "A change". "Also changes" is a disclosure with the
32	   full list.
33	6. **Designs show progress**: pages and how many approved or built, and when

1	// A project's architecture (prelude/architecture): a design of "kind":
2	// "architecture", one per project (R-p0j), kept as markdown files that agents
3	// read before they change anything (R-c2m) and that Prelude reads to show
4	// them on the project's Architecture pages (D-e8y). Nothing is written twice:
5	// the files are the one source, and what's derived (each part's "used by",
6	// decisions and findings, the map's layers) is prepared here.
7	//
8	// The files, in the design's architecture/ folder (the format the drafting
9	// agent is told: architecturePrompt in agent.js):
10	//
11	//   overview.md          # title, a summary, "## Layers" (a numbered list, top
12	//                        to bottom) and "## Principles" ("- **Title.** Why.")
13	//   parts/<id>.md        # title, then a header of "key: value" lines (layer,
14	//                        kind: module | process | outside, short, files: globs,
15	//                        uses: part ids), a summary, and "## Responsible for",
16	//                        "## Not its job", "## Owns" lists
17	//   decisions/<id>.md    # title, a header (status, date, parts, supersedes),
18	//                        then "## Context", "## Decision", "## Consequences"
19	//   flows/<id>.md        # title, a summary, numbered steps "part-id: text",
20	//                        and an optional "decisions:" header
21	//
22	// The check (R-4vx, R-k5e; D-r0k): after every turn that changes code, the
23	// code is read again - each file's imports (JavaScript and TypeScript, so
24	// far), each file mapped to its part by `files` - and these are reported: a
25	// use a part doesn't say it may make, a use of a part in a layer above, a
26	// code file no part names, and a named file that isn't there. A file is
27	// expected to belong to a part when it's under a folder a part's glob names
28	// (server/views/** covers server/views/, recursively), or beside a file a
29	// part names (server/main.js covers server/'s own files).

I've built the change. I couldn't run anything, so it hasn't been checked yet. Prelude's render after this turn will show whether every state still fits the model.

**What changed**
- **Views** (`server/views/projects/`):
  - `page.eta` is ported from the design. Its side column now starts with the Reference card.
  - `_designs.eta` is ported too. The architecture is now listed under Designs with an "Architecture" pill, a document icon and "14 parts and 9 decisions".
  - `_reference.eta` is new: it shows the design system and the architecture, each once it has something in it, and leaves out the app shell (R-x4b).
  - No styles were needed; the design adds none.
- **Model** (`server/project.js`):
  - `system` gains `components`, and the model gains `architecture` (`id`, `title`, `parts`, `decisions`, or null).
  - Designs gain `parts` and `decisions` for an architecture. Its stage is `approved` once it has parts, `designing` before.
  - Both are read wherever the design is: in main, or on its own branch while it's only there.
- **The design system link** (`server/main.js`): the card links to `/f/:project/system`, which the app didn't have. For now that URL redirects to the first screen of the design system's gallery. When the Prelude Design System design gives it a page of its own, that page replaces the redirect.
- **routes.json**: both routes and the POST answers now point at `@app/server/views/projects/…`, and the `from` lines are gone. The POST handlers already render `projects/page`, so their answers include the card without any handler changes.
- **RULES.md**: R-x4b's *proposed* line is removed. **NOTES.md** has a new "Built: Reference" section.

**What to look at before approving and opening the pull request**
- **The design system link.** It opens the gallery on the preview origin, not a reading page inside the app.
- **An architecture with parts but no overview counts as empty.** It counts nothing until its `overview.md` is written, because the Architecture pages show nothing before then. So the card won't link to a blank page, and its row under Designs says "nothing written yet". Check you're happy with that.
- **The four POST answers and the typical / large-project screens.** These should match your approved screens with the Reference card above The app.
